title: Benign tubular adenoma polyp
notice: Synthetic and AI-written. Needs review by a pathologist before being used to score anything (issue #22).

keys.span: The pathologist didn't see anything worrying.
keys.correct: The polyp was a tubular adenoma with low-grade dysplasia, with no high-grade dysplasia or cancer, and it was completely removed.
keys.source_hint: CAP colon and rectum protocol; pathology report
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: a benign polyp, but it could slowly turn into cancer over years if it were left alone
keys.correct: A tubular adenoma is a benign precancerous polyp that can slowly progress to cancer over years if not removed.
keys.source_hint: US Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: it was removed completely and showed no high-grade dysplasia
keys.correct: The adenoma was completely removed and had no high-grade dysplasia.
keys.source_hint: Pathology report; CAP colon and rectum protocol
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: So you won't ever need another colonoscopy.
keys.issue: Surveillance colonoscopy is still recommended after an adenoma.
keys.correct: Surveillance colonoscopy is still recommended. For one or two tubular adenomas under 10 mm, the next one is usually in 7 to 10 years.
keys.source_hint: US Multi-Society Task Force 2020 post-polypectomy surveillance
keys.speaker: doctor
